audit.whatIsWrong: Five of seven rows read 'Skill' and both ends of the chart are handed to Jax, while the page's own whys describe Urgot owning 1-5 and reclaiming the late game.
audit.why: The mirror set the chart to Urgot / Urgot / Skill / Urgot / Jax / Urgot / Urgot in both layers as one atomic group, and the packet chart agrees except on level 3 and first item. The content whys already describe exactly that shape, so only the enum rows were stale.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Urgot / Urgot / Skill / Urgot / Jax / Urgot / Urgot with ratings rescaled.

audit.whatIsWrong: Counter Strike is the focus of the whole page and never carries a number; whys[4] and whys[5] are also shifted a row out of step with their labels.
audit.why: Counter Strike is 17/15/13/11/9s at 300, Leap Strike 8/7.5/7/6.5/6s at 700, Empower 7/6/5/4/3s, Grandmaster-at-Arms 110/100/90s. Yours: Disdain 16s at rank 1, Purge 12/9/6/3/0s inside 490, Fear Beyond Death 100/85/70s. Row 4 is labelled Level 6 but whys[4] talked about level 5, and whys[5] (First item) described level 6.
audit.corrected: 17s written into the cooldown block, do-line and level-6 spike; whys[4] and whys[5] re-pointed at their own labels.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page says Fear Beyond Death 'executes him through his ult healing since it ignores his sustain'. Grandmaster-at-Arms has no healing. Also missing: Empower is an auto-attack reset.
audit.why: Riot's text for Grandmaster-at-Arms: every third consecutive attack deals bonus magic damage, and the active deals damage around him and increases his armour and magic resist. Resistances, not sustain — which makes Black Cleaver's shred the actual answer and turns the advice from a fiction into something checkable. Empower's reset means his burst opens on a wind-up, so that is the cue to step back rather than the cast.
audit.corrected: spikes[2] and late rewritten around the resistance buff; report[5].t now states the Empower reset.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Counterstrike' (one word) and 'Grandmaster's Might' are used throughout; neither is the ability's name.
audit.why: The kit file is authority on names: Counter Strike (E) and Grandmaster-at-Arms (R). Note that the mirror recorded renaming its occurrences to 'Grandmaster's Might', which disagrees with the kit — the kit was followed here and the conflict is flagged.
audit.corrected: All occurrences in the edited fields use Counter Strike and Grandmaster-at-Arms.

edits.after: Fear Beyond Death lands at 6, but so does Grandmaster-at-Arms, and its armour and magic resist blunt the trade that sets it up.

edits.before: Jax's real spike is level 6 Grandmaster's Might: with Counterstrike (E) already online he can walk into your W, dodge your autos, stun you, and burst. Do NOT full-commit here — respect the Counterstrike window, hold your E to interrupt his Leap Strike engage, and only trade when his E is down.
edits.after: Jax's real spike is level 6 Grandmaster-at-Arms: with Counter Strike already online — 17s at rank 1 — he walks into your Purge, dodges, stuns you and bursts. Do not full-commit here; hold Disdain for his Leap Strike engage and trade only once Counter Strike has been spent.

edits.before: Once you finish Bami's/Frostfire into tank shred you flip it back — kite his Counterstrike by walking away during its active, then re-engage with Q slow, W shred, and E to peel his re-Leap. Your R (Fear Beyond Death) executes him through his ult healing since it ignores his sustain once he's below threshold.
edits.after: Once your first tank-shred item is done you flip it back — walk away during Counter Strike's active, then re-engage with Corrosive Charge's slow, Purge, and Disdain for his re-Leap. Grandmaster-at-Arms grants armour and magic resist rather than healing, so Black Cleaver's shred is the direct answer to it.

edits.before: Jax has no defensive tool until his level 2 Counterstrike and no stun until it's leveled, so levels 1-2 are yours: shove, and punish every step-up with Corrosive Charge (Q) and a Purge (W) tick.
edits.after: Jax has no defensive tool until Counter Strike and no stun until it lands, so levels 1-2 are yours: shove, and punish every step-up with Corrosive Charge (Q) and a Purge (W) tick.

edits.before: Through levels 3-5 you own the lane by zoning his CS with Q and holding Disdain (E) for his Leap Strike; the one danger window is level 6, where Grandmaster's Might plus a ready Counterstrike lets him dodge your autos, stun you, and win a full commit.
edits.after: Through levels 3-5 you own the lane by zoning his CS with Corrosive Charge and holding Disdain for his Leap Strike, which is 8s at rank 1; the one danger window is level 6, where Grandmaster-at-Arms plus a ready Counter Strike lets him dodge, stun you and win a full commit.

edits.before: After your first tank-shred item the matchup swings back to you — W shreds his stacked resistances and R executes him through his ult healing — but a fed Jax still out-duels you at even gold, so use R to peel and pick rather than solo-bruising him.
edits.after: After your first tank-shred item the matchup swings back — Purge and Black Cleaver cut through the armour and magic resist Grandmaster-at-Arms grants, and your ult finishes anyone already under its threshold — but a fed Jax still out-duels you at even gold, so use R to peel and pick.

notes: Name conflict to resolve: the mirror renamed Jax's ult to 'Grandmaster's Might' in four places, but champ-data/_kits/jax.json — the stated authority on names — calls it Grandmaster-at-Arms. This audit follows the kit; if the mirror is left as-is the two pages will use different names for the same ability. suspectNames false positive: 'Counter Strike' in wants.you[0] is correct. Left untouched and unverified, as on the mirror: the page's description of Echoing Flames as percent-max-HP — Riot's text says only 'physical damage' and the kit carries no percentHealth flag. Also unasserted: whether Counter Strike's dodge applies to Purge, which is an ability rather than a basic attack.
